items.title: Stecher scores in final minute to lift Maple Leafs over Rangers
items.body: TORONTO — Troy Stecher scored with 26.3 seconds left in regulation as the Toronto Maple Leafs topped the New York Rangers 5-4 in a back-and-forth affair for their third straight victory Thursday. Brandon Duhaime, with a goal and two assists, Teddy Blueger, Kirill Marchenko and Easton Cowan provided the rest of the offence for Toronto (6-4-2). Sergei Bobrovsky made 21 saves. Zack MacEwen added two assists. Blueger also had an assist for a two-point night. Mika Zibanejad, with a goal and an assist, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Tye Kartye and Alexis Lafrenière replied for New York (7-4-1), which got 31 stops from Dylan Garand. Adam Fox chipped in four assists. Stecher's winner came on a delayed penalty after he took a pass from Morgan Rielly and ripped a shot upstairs. After the teams traded goals inside the game's first six minutes, Blueger put Toronto ahead with his first for the club at 10:01 on a shot that just dribbled over the line. New York evened things 2-2 at 2:37 of the second when Bjorkstrand beat Bobrovsky from in tight. The visitors nudged in front at 6:30 when Kartye tipped home a point shot, but Duhaime buried his own rebound 90 seconds later — also his first goal in blue and white — to get Toronto level again. Marchenko gave the home side the lead with 50 seconds left in the period on a power play, but Lafrenière knotted the score again at 14:25 of the third. Bobrovsky tied Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist for the most wins by a non-North American goaltender with 459. The pair now share sixth on the all-time list. items.summary: The San Jose Sharks picked up their first regulation win of the season Thursday night with a 6-2 win over the Ottawa Senators.
items.body: OTTAWA — The San Jose Sharks picked up their first regulation win of the season Thursday night with a 6-2 win over the Ottawa Senators . Colin Graf led the way with a goal and an assist. Nolan Allan, Tyler Toffoli, Jacob Trouba, Zack Ostapchuk and Ivar Stenberg also scored for the Sharks (6-4-1). Tim Stutzle and Jordan Spence tallied for the Senators (7-4-0). Samuel Ersson, who made 23 saves, remains in search of his first win with Ottawa. Ottawa placed Linus Ullmark on injured reserve Thursday after he suffered a lower-body injury a night earlier. Spence scored at 6:24 of the third period to make it a two-goal game. The Senators pulled Ersson while on the power play with under four minutes remaining but Ostapchuk took advantage of a giveaway and scored an empty-net goal. Stenberg added a second empty-netter to round out the scoring. Senators: Ottawa lacked the intensity it played with Wednesday against the Panthers and couldn’t bury its chances. Sharks: San Jose played a solid road game and capitalized on its opportunities. Toffoli broke a 1-1 tie at the halfway mark of the second period by getting a shot through traffic from the point on the power play. items.title: Save of the Season? Sharks' Askarov makes diving glove save to rob goal
items.summary:
Dive save and a beauty.
San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday.
The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck
items.body: San Jose Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov made an incredible diving glove save to stop a sure goal off a rocket from Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson at Canadian Tire Centre on Thursday. The Senators had a man advantage with defenseman Jake Sanderson controlling the puck at the point. Sanderson went cross-ice to forward Tim Stutzle at the right circle. Askarov moved to his left to play a shot from Stutzle, but he opted to go back across the ice to Batherson, who had a pretty open net. Askarov, a right-hand catcher, made a huge dive to his right and snagged Batherson's shot out of midair. Even with some traffic in front of the net, Askarov was still able to get there with the dive, looking more like a Gold Glove shortstop than a hockey goalie. Earlier in the game, Askarov made a pretty nice pad save on a Shane Pinto breakaway chance. After the diving save, he laid on the ice for a second and waited for the whistle. Take the rest, Yaroslav. You earned it.

Jets Hockey Development (JHD) Girls Learn to Play is the first program of its kind in Winnipeg specifically for girls aged 6 to 10 who are new to hockey. Participants received on-ice instruction by an all-woman coaching staff, equipment support and connections to local minor hockey associations and girls’ hockey programs, creating a pathway to continued participation in the sport. The program officially launched Sept. 2 at hockey for all centre with a welcome event for 40 girls and their families. items.title: Golden Knights’ Mitch Marner to miss game vs. Blues for birth of child
items.summary: The 29-year-old and his wife Stephanie Marner are set to welcome their second child.
items.body: Forward Mitch Marner will be unavailable for the Vegas Golden Knights on the road for their Thursday night game against the St. Louis Blues as he and his partner, Stephanie Marner, await the birth of their second child. The team confirmed his status ahead of puck drop, after the Las Vegas Review-Journal reported that Marner and his wife were expecting the newborn. The Marner’s first child was born in May 2025, Miles Daniel Marner, with the birth happening just before Game 1 of the round two Stanley Cup Playoff series against the Florida Panthers, when Mitch was still a member of the Toronto Maple Leafs. Now in his second season with the Golden Knights, the 29-year-old Marner has a pair of goals and 10 assists for 11 points in 11 regular season games this season, as he looks to build on his 24 goals, 56 assists and 80-point campaign from last season’s 81 games and eventual advancement to the Stanley Cup Final. In his place for Thursday’s contest, Alexander Holtz is set to draw into the lineup for his NHL season debut. The 24-year-old native of Stockholm, Sweden, played in 28 games with the Golden Knights last season, scoring three goals and six assists for nine points. This season, he has enjoyed a strong start in the AHL with the Henderson Silver Knights, scoring four goals and four assists for eight points in eight games. Vegas enter Thursday’s road matchup with the Blues sitting first in the Western Conference’s Pacific Division with an 8-3-0 record, and will be back on the ice on the road against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night before returning home to T-Mobile Arena for a pair of home games next week against the Ottawa Senators and New Jersey Devils .

items.title: Red Wings looking for young centres in trade talks
items.body: The Detroit Red Wings appear to be letting teams know what it could take to acquire their two unhappy superstars. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Thursday's episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast that the Red Wings are seeking young centres in trade talks for Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson . "Detroit, whatever they're considering out there, whether it's Larkin or Edvinsson ... but the one thing I think they are doing, and I've heard this a little bit, is they're starting to ask about young centres. And maybe some guys who are top prospects who aren't in the NHL yet. I had a couple of teams tell me on Wednesday ... whatever Detroit is planning here, they're looking at young centres." Friedman added that he couldn't say if the conversations were related to Larkin, Edvinsson or both. "I've had a couple of teams say to me do not be surprised if and when this logjam breaks, if one or two (centres) are involved for Detroit if they can. That is definitely a goal of theirs," he said. Larkin, 30, is a centre who has been on the market since he requested a trade at the end of last season. He holds a no-trade clause but a recent report from The Detroit Free Press revealed that the former Red Wings captain has expanded the list of teams he is open to joining to 10. The Red Wings have had trouble building centre depth behind Larkin over the course of their 10-year playoff drought. Currently the team is leaning heavily on Andrew Copp and Larkin, while sophomore Emmitt Finnie has moved from wing to centre. Meanwhile, recent first-round picks Marco Kasper and Nate Danielson have had their development slowed by injuries and neither is contributing to the team right now. items.body: Register Login East Notes: Chatfield, Cousins, Tkachuk By Ethan Hetu | at October 22, 2026 6:35 pm The Carolina Hurricanes did a remarkable job retaining nearly the entirety of their Stanley Cup-winning roster from last season. But with another year set to go by, it seems almost certain that the club will lose at least some players from their championship roster. One player that could depart is pending UFA defenseman Jalen Chatfield . David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period reported yesterday that the Hurricanes and Chatfield’s agent, Darren Ferris of Quartexx, attempted to negotiate an extension, but those talks did not result in pen hitting paper. Pagnotta noted that there “have been no talks since” between Ferris and the Hurricanes, and added that the “inkling right now is that [Chatfield] is headed to free agency.” Chatfield, could be set to cash in on the open market after becoming a steady contributor to the Hurricanes’ defense over the last half-decade. A fleet-footed undrafted blueliner, Chatfield was plucked from the Canucks organization as a free agent and broke into the NHL after one season spent developing with Carolina’s AHL affiliate, the Chicago Wolves. After winning a Calder Cup in Chicago, Chatfield established himself at the NHL level. He was a seamless fit for the way head coach Rod Brind’Amour wants his defensemen to play, and his ability to leverage his above-average skating to close out on pucks quickly and play aggressively has made him a valuable secondary defensive piece for the club. Now 30 years old, Chatfield’s upcoming free agency represents his best chance at earning a life-changing contract. Based on Pagnotta’s reporting, it seems Chatfield might end up receiving that contract, just maybe not from the Hurricanes.

items.title: Panthers’ Cooper Black becomes tallest goalie to play NHL game
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Florida Panthers goalie Cooper Black skated onto the PPG Paints Arena ice alone during pregame warmups on Thursday night, a time-honoured hockey tradition given to rookies everywhere. It took Black fewer strides to make the memorable lap than most. Black made NHL history in his first career start when he became the tallest goaltender to ever appear in a regular-season game. Black is listed as two inches taller than Ben Bishop, Ivan Fedotov, Mads Sogaard and Mikko Koskinen, all 6-foot-7. The 25-year-old from Alpen, Michigan, who started playing when he was 8 and had a 5-inch growth spurt between his junior and senior years in high school when he shot up from 6 feet to 6 feet 5 inches and kept right on going, was excellent in his first period. Black, called up from Florida's AHL affiliate in Charlotte recently after Jacob Markstrom went down with a shoulder injury, stopped Pittsburgh Penguins defenseman Kris Letang with his blocker pad on a wrist shot about two minutes in. He also turned aside a breakaway opportunity by Penguins forward Rickard Rakell before giving up a goal to Nick Robertson, who beat Black to the glove side. Panthers head coach Paul Maurice praised Black's development in recent years. Florida signed Black as an undrafted rookie free agent in 2024. Black blossomed last season in Charlotte, posting a 25-13-4 record with a 2.47 goals against average and a .903 save percentage. “A man that size, it takes a long time to grow into that body,” Maurice said before adding with a laugh, “I think he’s done.”

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A significant milestone has been reached…both literally and figuratively. On Thursday night, Florida Panthers goaltender Cooper Black made his NHL debut against the Pittsburgh Penguins , making him the tallest goaltender in league history. Black stands head-and-shoulders above a lot of his competition. Coming in at 6-foot-9, the 25-year-old surpasses Ben Bishop and Ivan Fedotov, who were both 6-foot-7 during their days in the NHL. The undrafted goaltender was called up from Florida’s American Hockey League affiliate, the Charlotte Checkers, earlier this week after fellow backstop Jacob Markstrom went down with an injury during practice. Markstrom was later revealed to be ruled out for the next 10-14 days, leading to Panthers head coach Paul Maurice stating that Black would get his first shot in the big time sometime during the team’s four-game road trip. Black has been solid in his first few appearances with Charlotte this season, going 2-1-0 with a 2.67 goals-against average and a .919 save percentage. He stopped 33 of the 35 shots he faced last Saturday in a 4-2 victory over the Hartford Wolf Pack, the New York Rangers’ primary affiliate. The Alpena, Mich. native is coming off an impressive second full season with the Checkers, where he went 25-13-4, helping his team finish third in the AHL’s Atlantic Division. Most hockey fans remember Ron Duguay as a the perfectly coiffed cult star of the New York Rangers . And he deserves all of the recognition he gets as one of the most popular players in franchise history. But Duguay, who died of cancer at the age of 69 on Wednesday, was even more popular and dynamic as a member of the Sudbury Wolves in the mid-1970s, when he led a team that did everything but win an Ontario League championship. That was where he first displayed his blazing speed, on-ice elegance and soft touch before being drafted by the Rangers in the first round of the 1977 draft. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Positive news for the Minnesota Wild as they continue their road trip through Western Canada. The team activated captain Jared Spurgeon from injured reserve, making him available to be in the lineup on Thursday night, when the Wild visit the Calgary Flames . It will be the veteran defenseman’s first action in four games. He was placed on IR with an upper-body injury on Sunday, retroactive to Oct. 12, when he helped the Wild pick up a win over the Vegas Golden Knights. With Spurgeon out of the lineup, the Wild held firm, but weren’t amazing. They fell to the surprising Winnipeg Jets before beating the St. Louis Blues seven days ago. Then, after beating the Columbus Blue Jackets on Sunday, Minnesota managed to rally from a 3-1 deficit to salvage a point against the Edmonton Oilers , only to lose in overtime. In Minnesota’s first six games of the 2026-27 campaign, the 36-year-old scored a goal and four assists for five points, tied for fifth on the team in helpers. Spurgeon has a plus/minus of +4, while averaging 22:21 of ice time. Staying in the lineup and out of the press box has been tough for Spurgeon throughout his NHL career. Only one of the Edmonton native’s 17 seasons saw him appear in every game, that coming during the 2018-19 campaign. He did play in 79 games last year, which came just two years after Spurgeon was limited to a mere 16 contests. In 1.018 regular-season games in the NHL, Spurgeon has posted 124 goals and 319 assists for 443 points, with another 31 points in 84 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. items.body: TORONTO -- Dave Maloney was never surprised to see how Ron Duguay valiantly fought his battle with cancer. It was with a positive attitude and a zest for life that had come to define the way Duguay lived until he died Thursday at the age of 69. “It was commendable, it was commendable to his family,” Maloney told NHL.com on Thursday. “His daughters really, and his son, his family, were really the basis for his fight. We're culturally, as hockey guys, we're not going to give up, right? I just think that it was admirable but I wouldn't expect anything other than that from who I knew him to be when we were all young.” Maloney and Duguay were teammates with the New York Rangers for six seasons, from 1977-83, which began when Maloney was 21 and Duguay was 20. Maloney said Duguay, and Dave’s brother, Don, who joined the Rangers for the 1978-79 season, stood out to him for being on the forefront of physical fitness during an era where the expectations that players face today were not the same. “He and my brother were two guys that were ahead of the curve believe it or not, in taking care of themself,” Maloney said. “I know the dynamic story of Ron and there's a lot of reality to those dynamic stories, believe me, but he took care of himself. He really did. He was physically fit. His father was a fitness guy. items.body: 19-year-old forward lost consciousness, still 'clearly shaken,' GM says CRANBERRY, Pa. -- Ben Kindel could return to practice as soon as next week after losing consciousness aboard the Pittsburgh Penguins team plane Tuesday, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday. The 19-year-old forward was cleared to travel to Pittsburgh on Wednesday after experiencing a vasovagal syncope, a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure that reduces blood flow to the brain, about 10 minutes after the plane departed Salt Lake City International Airport. Kindel received oxygen before an emergency medical landing and was transported to the University of Utah medical center. Kindel, who played 18:53 in a 5-4 loss at the Utah Mammoth on Monday, was placed on injured reserve Thursday. He will have increased testing and could begin training in the next four days if there are no complications, Dubas said. "I mean, so tough to put a timeframe on it," Dubas said. "We play tonight. We play Saturday night. ... Our hope is to get everything done, tested, back into training here in the next four days or so and see if he can return to practice on Sunday or Monday. "That's why I would put an asterisk on that by saying 'we'll see how everything goes before then.'" Kindel has four points (two goals, two assists) in nine games this season, his second since being selected by Pittsburgh in the first round (No. 11) of the 2025 NHL Draft. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Well, this isn’t the best news if you’re a Montreal Canadiens fan. On Thursday, the team announced that captain Nick Suzuki will be out 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. In response, the team has called up forward Owen Beck from its American Hockey League affiliate, the Laval Rocket. While the team didn’t specify what exactly is keeping Suzuki out until November, the injury can be traced back to what happened during the Canadiens’ matchup against the San Jose Sharks on Tuesday night. In the latter half of regulation, the 27-year-old blocked a shot with his left hand, leaving him shaken up. However, Suzuki would fight through the pain, playing the remainder of the contest, which saw Montreal fall 4-3 in overtime. Not lost in Suzuki’s injury is that his career-long iron man streak will come to an end. Since first stepping onto NHL ice with the Habs during the 2019-20 campaign, Suzuki has appeared in every single one of his team’s games in both the regular season and the Stanley Cup Playoffs. He has played 546 consecutive regular-season contests, with another 56 in the postseason. Yet, Montreal will have to navigate the next few weeks, including a four-game road trip, without their on-ice leader. In nine games so far, the London, Ont. native has scored five goals and seven assists for 12 points, sitting tied for the team lead in helpers and second in goals. Beck has appeared in two games with Montreal this season, but has yet to register a point. In five games with Laval, the 22-year-old has posted a goal and an assist. items.title: Penguins’ Ben Kindel back in Pittsburgh after collapsing on team plane
items.body: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after collapsing on the team's plane on Tuesday. General manager Kyle Dubas told reporters on Thursday that Kindel suffered a vasovagal episode — a sudden drop in heart rate and blood pressure reducing blood flow to the brain — about 10 minutes after departing from Utah and regained consciousness after receiving oxygen from the team's medical staff. The plane made an emergency landing and Kindel was transported to the University of Utah medical centre. He was cleared to fly back to Pittsburgh on Wednesday, travelling with Nick Bonino, Jason Spezza and two team doctors. The Penguins placed the 19-year-old on injured reserve as he undergoes more testing at the team facilities. Dubas said the team hopes to get Kindel back to training within the next four days and practicing next week, depending on the results of his testing. Dubas said Kindel had no prior history of collapsing. "We will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben," Dubas said. "That's our primary goal and paramount to his future and health." The Coquitlam, B.C., native is in his second year with the Penguins. In nine games, Kindel has two goals and two assists. He played nearly 19 minutes during a loss to Utah on Monday night.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-US PRESSWIRE One of the game’s most iconic figures has died. On Thursday, it was announced that former NHLer Ron Duguay passed away at the age of 69 following a two-year cancer battle. The news was broken by Duguay’s girlfriend, former Alaska governor and 2008 vice presidential candidate, Sarah Palin. While Duguay may not have had hall-of-fame numbers or Stanley Cup rings, his legacy will remain one of hockey’s first stars to transcend the game, diving into popular culture with the New York Rangers during the disco-crazed 1970s. The Val Caron, Ont. native was drafted by the Rangers with the 13th overall pick of the 1977 NHL Draft, just a few months after winning a silver medal with Canada at the IIHF World Junior Championship. He immediately joined a strong team in New York that had the likes of Rod Gilbert, Phil Esposito and John Davidson. Duguay was a key part of the Rangers’ run to the Stanley Cup Final in 1979, where the Blueshirts fell to the Montreal Canadiens dynasty in five games. While he might be well-known as a Ranger on the ice, spending parts of eight seasons with the Original Six franchise, Duguay’s reputation on the ice made him a household name. A frequent visitor to the famous Studio 54, the former Sudbury Wolves star fit right into NYC nightlife, with his long, curly hair making him a sort of sex symbol. He even had a brief fling with Cher in the later years of the decade. In 1980, Duguay was featured in legendary artist Andy Warhol’s “Athletes” portrait series, which included other famous athletes such as Muhammad Ali and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. items.title: Former NHL player Ron Duguay dies at 69 after a bout with cancer
items.body: NEW YORK — Ron Duguay, who played nearly 1,000 games in the NHL from the late 1970s through the ’80s, has died of cancer. He was 69. A spokesperson for the New York Rangers said Thursday that Duguay's family informed the team of his death. Duguay played his first six seasons with the New York Rangers after they selected him with the 13th pick in the draft in 1977. The Sudbury, Ontario, native was an All-Star as a point-a-game producer in 1981-82. A series of trades led him to spend time with the Detroit Red Wings, Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings with another Rangers stint, as well. Duguay finished his career in the league with 673 points in the regular season and playoffs, then played in Germany and the minors. Duguay was known late in life away from hockey for dating former Alaska governor and 2008 Republican U.S. vice presidential nominee Sarah Palin. His family started a GoFundMe earlier this year to offset the costs of travel and treatments. “It’s with a shattered heart but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now,” Palin posted on social media. “He fought so hard. Love never ends.”

items.summary: When Brady Tkachuk returned to Ottawa as a despised member of the Panthers, Senators fans unleashed their combative spirit, bringing a level of sustained savagery that would make even the most vindictive fanbases proud.
items.body: KANATA, Ont. — For years, Ottawa Senators fans watched Brady Tkachuk bring the fight to opponents. When he returned to Ottawa as a despised member of the Florida Panthers, they unleashed their own combative spirit, bringing a level of sustained savagery that would make even the most vindictive fanbases proud. Sens supporters were merciless on their former captain on Wednesday night, as Tkachuk — who was traded to the Florida Panthers in June after informing Ottawa he would not sign another contract with the team — returned for the first time to the city he called home for eight seasons. The Canadian Tire Centre in Kanata throbbed with an energy worthy of a Game 7, as emotions pent up for months — maybe even longer — spilled onto the ice like blood after a brawl. While the start of the game was marked by rigorous boos, the end featured what remained of an announced sellout crowd gleefully cheering as the final seconds ticked away in a thunderous 5-1 Ottawa win. A couple events — Tkachuk himself scoring on Florida’s first shot of the contest and Sens goalie Linus Ullmark being forced out of the game with a lower-body strain in the third — threatened to sap the masses of their zealous desire to deride. items.summary: Tkachuk previously stated that he would donate any sweaters tossed on the ice to the local Boys & Girls Club.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Fans in the nation’s capital made their voices heard and ultimately got the last laugh. During a break in the action in the third period of the highly anticipated matchup between the Florida Panthers and Ottawa Senators , Senators fans found an opportunity to dispose of some leftover Brady Tkachuk jerseys, and dozens of sweaters from the former Ottawa captain flew over the glass and onto the ice at the Canadian Tire Centre on Wednesday night. The public display of disapproval might’ve been sparked by a scuffle involving the Tkachuk brothers, as the two got into it with many of Brady’s former teammates in front of the Ottawa bench, leading to roughing minors for the infamous duo. Senators supporters throwing jerseys on the ice was somewhat expected heading into Wednesday’s contest. After morning skate, Tkachuk told reporters he would donate any jersey thrown onto the ice to the Boys & Girls Club of Ottawa, where the 27-year-old volunteered during his time with the Sens. The players wearing the current Sens logo were sure not to let the moment overcome them, as the team put forth a dominating effort. Despite Tkachuk scoring the first goal of the game, Ottawa stormed back with five unanswered goals, coming away with a 5-1 victory. Tkachuk finished the game with a -2 plus/minus and four penalty minutes. The jersey-throwing was only part of the patrons’ antics throughout the contest. Chants of “Brady sucks,” and “F— you, Brady” came down from the rafters every time Tkachuk was on the ice. It was the fans’ first time seeing their former captain play against the Sens since he requested a trade this past offseason , with Ottawa sending him to Florida for three first-round picks and a second-round pick.

items.body: BUFFALO, N.Y. — Rookie forward Cole Knuble scored twice to help the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Buffalo Sabres 3-1 on Wednesday night. Knuble, playing his second career game, scored his first two goals in front of his father, former NHL forward Mike Knuble, who played 1,068 games with five teams. Trevor Zegras also scored and Dan Vladar made 27 saves to give the Flyers their third straight win after starting 0-6-3. Jason Zucker made his season debut following sports hernia surgery and scored for Buffalo. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 23 shots for the Sabres, who are 1-1-2 in their last four games. Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin returned to the lineup after missing four games with an upper-body injury. The Flyers grabbed a 2-0 lead late in the first period after Knuble’s first career goal at 14:49 and a power-play goal from Zegras at 19:17 when he batted a rebound of Matvei Michkov’s shot out of the air past Luukkonen. Zucker’s power-play goal at 19:25 of the second cut it to 2-1. Knuble’s second of the game 3:03 into the third made it 3-1 after he banked in the puck off Luukkonen’s skate. Flyers forward Tyson Foerster returned to the lineup after a one-game absence because of an undisclosed injury. Both teams are in action again Saturday. The Sabres open a four-game trip against the Washington Capitals, while the Flyers return home to host the Anaheim Ducks.

items.title: Senators’ Linus Ullmark exits vs. Panthers with apparent injury
items.body: The Ottawa Senators once again lost their starting netminder to an apparent injury on Wednesday against the Florida Panthers. Linus Ullmark had to be helped off by a trainer and teammate Claude Giroux after staying down on the ice following a third-period save. The stop came on a shot off the rush from former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk. But as the rebound went to an Ottawa defenceman and down to the Florida end, Ullmark hunched over in pain as officials blew the play dead. As the Senators goalie was tended to in his crease, a scrum broke out in front of the Ottawa bench while the home fans continued their game-long chant of "Brady sucks" and threw Tkachuk jerseys on the ice. Ullmark had stopped 16 of the 17 shots he faced before exiting. This is the second time this month that the 33-year-old wasn't able to finish a start after leaving early against the Boston Bruins on Oct. 5. Senators head coach Travis Green said Ullmark "tweaked something a little bit" in that outing against Boston. Ullmark entered Wednesday's game with a 6-1-0 record on the season with a 1.33 goals-against average and .945 save percentage.

items.title: Canucks GM Ryan Johnson preaching patience as losses pile up
items.summary: With the rebuilding Canucks on an eight-game losing streak, GM Ryan Johnson isn’t panicking. “Before it gets better, it was going to get really hard, and we have to understand that.”
items.body: VANCOUVER — The evening before training camp opened, general manager Ryan Johnson gathered the Vancouver Canucks ’ staff and players for a dinner meeting at the team’s lakeside hotel in Penticton, and then spoke the truth. “The No. 1 thing I talked about is: ‘You have no idea how hard this is going to be,’” Johnson recalled Wednesday. “Like, ‘what you've signed up for here is almost impossible.’ You’d be ignorant... if you thought you were just going to walk in and things would fall into place. I said: ‘You’ve got to be ready because you're going to get punched in the face real quick.’ Here they are, bruised and spiralling through an eight-game losing streak and just 2-8-1 through the start of the rebuild’s first full season. In their last five games, Vancouver has been tied or led four times through 40 minutes and trailed (by a goal) once, then been outscored 11-0 in the third period while losing all of them. The rebuild is not the impossible part that Johnson referred to just five weeks ago, although there is overwhelming evidence around the National Hockey League — see the Detroit Red Wings, the Canucks’ opponents Thursday — that it will be difficult. The impossible part is believing the Canucks, under new management, with new coaches and new systems, many young and new players, and lofty organizational priorities regarding culture and environment, would somehow come out of the gate and be successful competitively against a murderer’s row of initial opponents. In seven of their first 11 games, the Canucks have faced a team that has either won the Stanley Cup or been to the final in the last five years. And like 7-Eleven, the Canucks’ team defence has been open at all hours, surrendering an NHL-worst 51 goals. As Johnson predicted, they have been punched in the face.

On Wednesday night, after a few months of waiting, the Ottawa faithful had their chance to let their former captain know how they felt about his decision. items.summary: It’s been more than three months since Blake Coleman was traded to the Minnesota Wild, but the Texas native still has a little Calgary left in him. Eric Francis looks back at what made Coleman’s time with the Flames so special ahead of his return to Calgary on Thursday.
items.body: CALGARY – Blake Coleman came to Calgary without cowboy boots. Five years later, he owned a pair bought specifically for the Stampede, his young daughters were saying “zed” instead of “zee,” and the occasional “kilometres” was slipping into family conversations. The Texas native may have left the Flames this summer, but Canada clearly isn’t done with him yet. “Oh man, definitely not comfortable with kilometres - I still don’t know how to convert those,” said Coleman, laughing. “But I do say ‘eh’ a lot. My family calls me out from time to time.” The boots, the Canadian vocabulary, the Christmases spent in Banff, and the Montana property he’s building a couple of hours down the road from his former hockey home are all reminders of just how much the city got under his skin. “I guess that’s kind of a permanent impression that it left on us,” said Coleman, who returns to Calgary Thursday night for his first game against the Flames since being traded to Minnesota in the off-season. “I don’t think I ever would have discovered Whitefish if we hadn’t been playing there.” That’s quite the legacy for a hockey town sometimes accused of being a little too cold, a little too remote and a little too attached to an aging arena. “I still remember my first impression when you walked in,” said Coleman. “You kind of feel like you walked into a junior hockey locker room.” But five years of memories have a funny way of changing your perspective. “The more you’re there, the more you almost kind of appreciate it, and find things that you like about it. I think that’s just kind of it - it just felt like home for five years,” he said. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images The trade request saga between three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goalie Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets could either be resolved or reach a new pinnacle of drama soon. "I'm loving it a lot more," said Vlasic. " I've been with her everyday ... it's cool to see the evolution of it. (She's) starting to crawl, starting to motor quite a bit now, so I got my hands full." items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Not the most promising news in the U.S. capital. With Quinn due for a new contract soon, how will the Sabres navigate his future? After making the playoffs for the first time in 15 years, the Buffalo Sabres lost two key members of their core group over the summer in winger Alex Tuch and defenseman Bowen Byram. Sabres GM Jarmo Kekalainen chose not to make any significant acquisitions other than blueliner Olen Zellweger during the summer, and gambled that the club's group of emerging youngsters would be able to make up for the offensive gap created by Tuch and Byram's departure. Nearly a month into the season, only a few of Buffalo's young cadre have been effective in picking up the slack. The most successful of which is winger Jack Quinn. Because of the COVID pandemic and the OHL being shut down, the winger played in the American Hockey League as a 19-year-old.
